The initial EUI (55.6 kBtu/ft²) was calculated using the Tribal Office utility bills from the pre-retrofit period. These data form the basis for evaluating the effectiveness of the retrofits over time. Energy use intensity per heating degree day (EUI/HDD) was reported in terms of annual kBtu/ft2 for the available calendar years for the building. EUI/HDD is the annual energy usage first normalized by the conditioned floor area of the building and normalized again by the base 65°F HDD for the observed year. HDDs are the cumulative difference in daily mean temperature from a baseline temperature. More heating degree days occur in colder locations and generally correlate to higher energy usage. EUI/HDD was calculated using actual heating degree data from the Bethel Airport weather station (60°46’47.0″ N, 161°50’16.0″ W; elevation 125 ft), obtained via the Alaska Climate Research Center’s Data Portal, which provides an interactive interface to the United States Department of Commerce, National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration’s weather records. Bethel was used as the reference station because Akiachak is too small to have its own weather station. Energy cost index (ECI) was reported in terms of annual dollars per square foot for the available calendar years. ECI is the annual utility costs for electricity and fuel oil normalized by the conditioned floor area of the building. PCE is funded through investment earnings from the PCE Endowment Fund, which is managed by the Alaska Permanent Fund Corporation.
